_comment: Single source of truth for drills (design doc section 5). code = station code shown on signs, cues and logs (B build, P piece control, E edit). Steps are actions, never raw keys. advance = [right, forward, up] cells between reps (each rep gets a fresh track). lane = geometry for tools/build_map.py: kind gap (catch floor one level below the cells in front) or flat, forward/up = cells the drill needs. principle = id from principles; why = one plain-language reason shown before the set; reflect = one question shown after it; tip = one coaching sentence shown on the results card when a set is not clean (no quotes, braces or backslashes). check kind exposure = the step fails if the player takes damage during that step's window (needs a pressure source, see design/training-ground-spec.md). Run tools/gen_drills.py after editing. loadout = melee means the lane pad strips weapons and consumables (pickaxe and materials stay) so the player practises movement and building without a gun; default is any. Check kind target_hit needs the drill device's GunHit or PickaxeHit trigger wired to a target's hit event (see design/training-ground-spec.md).

audio_cues.arena_ready: Both players, step onto a platform. Press start when you're ready.
audio_cues.arena_reset: Round over. Return to your platform.
audio_cues.piece_control_brief: Build your cover. Move through the tunnel. Control the next box before you open a peek.

action_hints.wall: Crosshair at chest height on the tile edge you want to block.
action_hints.floor: Look slightly down: crosshair on the tile edge just ahead of your feet.
action_hints.ramp: Face the way you will climb, crosshair on the next tile.
action_hints.cone: Look up so the crosshair is overhead, then place the roof.
action_hints.edit: Edit aim: middle of the wall at chest height. A window is the centre tile.
action_hints.edit_confirm: Confirm while the crosshair is still on the chosen tiles.
action_hints.reset: Reset right after the peek so the wall is whole again.
action_hints.jump: Jump as you place, not before.
action_hints.turn_right: Flick to the next wall while you are in the air.
action_hints.fire: Fire once the crosshair is on the target, not before.
action_hints.swap_weapon: One press of your gun slot, then fire.
action_hints.pickaxe: One press of your pickaxe slot.

principles.name: Accuracy before speed
principles.rule: Use a pace where you can place the intended piece, then test it faster.
principles.why: Controlled practice makes aim and placement errors easier to notice. Faster reps test whether the movement holds under time pressure.
principles.creative: Use your own binds and building settings. Adjust the pace when accuracy drops, and include movement once placement is reliable.

principles.name: Cover the threat
principles.rule: Identify the threat direction and place useful cover before exposing yourself.
principles.why: A wall helps only when it blocks the relevant angle. Cover placement and your position work together.
principles.creative: Choose the piece and order for the threat, terrain and route. A drill sequence is one setup to practise, not a rule for every fight.

principles.name: Check before opening
principles.rule: Check the exposed angles before opening an edit toward the threat.
principles.why: An edit changes who can see and shoot you. Cover on the other sides helps isolate the angle you intend to take.
principles.creative: Choose the opening and timing for the situation. Keep a route back to cover instead of enclosing yourself without an exit.

principles.name: Recover cover
principles.rule: After a peek, decide whether to reset, reposition or continue the safe angle.
principles.why: A reset can close a return-shot angle. Repositioning may be better when the piece is weak or another side is threatened.
principles.creative: This drill practises resetting after the peek. In a fight, reassess the threat instead of repeating the sequence automatically.

principles.name: Check piece control
principles.rule: Check control of the piece before relying on its edit.
principles.why: An edit plan depends on access to the piece and a usable angle. Piece control supports the plan but does not guarantee a safe peek.
principles.creative: Choose whether to contest, defend or move to another cell. Track the opponent and your escape route while you build.

principles.name: Read the peek
principles.rule: Use cover and crosshair placement, then adapt if the opponent reads your angle.
principles.why: Repeated timing can become predictable. A useful peek depends on exposure, target position and whether the opponent is ready.
principles.creative: Repeat a stable setup while learning it. Add different angles and timing once you can return to cover reliably.

principles.name: Right tool, ready early
principles.rule: Prepare the item for the next action while maintaining useful cover.
principles.why: A deliberate swap reduces time spent correcting the selected item and keeps attention on the target.
principles.creative: Use a comfortable inventory layout and your preferred input method. Practise finding the intended item without unnecessary cycling.

drills.name: Wall (front)
drills.tip: Aim at the intended wall cell, check the build preview, and place one wall with your normal build controls.
drills.why: This isolates wall placement so you can connect crosshair position, preview and the piece that appears.
drills.reflect: Did the wall occupy the intended cell and cover the angle you chose?

drills.name: Floor (front)
drills.tip: Aim into the intended floor cell and check the preview before committing your movement.
drills.why: Floor placement and movement must agree so the landing surface is where you expect it.
drills.reflect: Did the floor appear in the intended cell before you moved onto it?

drills.name: Ramp (forward)
drills.tip: Check the ramp preview and climb direction before moving onto it.
drills.why: A correctly placed ramp needs the intended cell and orientation, not just a gain in height.
drills.reflect: Did the ramp face the intended route, or did you correct it after moving?

drills.name: Cone
drills.tip: Aim at the intended cell and check the cone preview before placing it.
drills.why: Cones can control space or provide cover. Their placement order depends on the setup and the threat.
drills.reflect: Did the cone occupy the cell you meant to control?

drills.name: Piece switching
drills.tip: For this exercise, switch wall, floor, ramp, cone while keeping each preview in its intended cell.
drills.why: A fixed sequence isolates the transitions between pieces. Other situations need different orders.
drills.reflect: Which transition moved your crosshair away from the intended cell?

drills.name: Ramp rush
drills.tip: For this exercise, alternate wall and ramp while checking front cover and the next climb.
drills.why: This sequence practises gaining height with front cover. Side angles still need attention.
drills.reflect: Where did you lose front cover or place the next ramp off your route?
drills.basis: Completepatrick: layer walls in front while advancing, simple wall-ramp combos. Ramp-first is accepted.

drills.name: Wall, ramp, floor
drills.tip: For this exercise, place wall, ramp, floor and check the cell and orientation of each piece.
drills.why: The sequence connects front cover, a climb and a landing surface. Placement quality matters more than completing the inputs.
drills.reflect: Which piece missed its intended cell or left an angle exposed?
drills.basis: Derived from the cover-first principle; no direct source for the exact order.

drills.name: Protected ramp
drills.tip: Check the threat side and add the side wall before moving into the exposed part of this route.
drills.why: Side cover can protect the climb, but only if its position matches the threat angle.
drills.reflect: Was the threat side covered as you moved onto the floor?
drills.basis: Derived from cover-first. Guides describe ramp then two side walls then a front wall for a one-sided climb, which is accepted.

drills.name: Tunnel run
drills.tip: Repeat floor, side walls and cone for every open cell until you reach the goal ledge. Stepping onto the goal ends the rep.
drills.why: A tunnel is moving cover. The floor gives footing, the side walls stop flanking shots, and the cone keeps fire from above out.
drills.reflect: Which angle stayed exposed while you moved into the next cell?
drills.basis: Guides agree on floor, walls around you, then a roof, then edit the front to go on. Cone-first and wall-ramp tunnels are accepted. Sources disagree on one canonical order (secondary guides, not verified in the live game), so the reference is one valid order and accepts lists the others.

drills.name: Box up
drills.tip: Floor for footing, a wall toward the threat, a floor overhead, then close the other three sides.
drills.why: Each piece has a job: the floor gives you footing, the first wall blocks the shot you can see, the overhead floor stops a build-over, and the last walls finish the box.
drills.reflect: Did you know the threat direction and your next exit before enclosing the cell?
drills.basis: Reference order set by the project owner (floor, wall, floor, then close the other walls). Four walls then floor and cone, wall-wall-floor-ramp and wall-floor-cone appear in guides and are accepted.

drills.name: 90s
drills.tip: Two walls, jump, floor then ramp underneath, then turn into the next 90.
drills.why: This isolated sequence practises gaining height through a turn. Compare the pieces and landing, not just the jump height.
drills.reflect: Did the turn leave your crosshair on the next placement or inside an obstructing piece?
drills.basis: Two walls, jump, then floor and ramp underneath, then turn into the next 90 (Voicetube, GGRecon). Red Bull and Gamertag Mythras describe slightly different orders; those are accepted. Sources disagree on one canonical order (secondary guides, not verified in the live game), so the reference is one valid order and accepts lists the others.

drills.name: Tunnel and window
drills.tip: Seal the tunnel (floor, sides, roof) before you edit. Open one side window for a sightline, then reset it at once.
drills.why: Checking the other angles before opening an edit helps keep attention on the threat you intend to face.
drills.reflect: Which other angle was exposed while the window was open?
drills.basis: Tunnel part follows tunnel. Edit a window for a sightline and reset it: FullBoosts and Boosteria.

drills.name: Box and re-box
drills.tip: Build the box, peek and reset, then replace any wall that took damage before you do anything else.
drills.why: Recovering cover can mean a reset, repair or movement into another cell. This sequence isolates the reset and next wall.
drills.reflect: After the peek, would holding this cell or moving give you better cover?
drills.basis: Box part follows box_up. Peek, reset and replace-the-damaged-wall come from the FullBoosts and Boosteria guides.

drills.name: Door edit
drills.tip: Create the intended door opening, confirm it with your edit settings, and move through under control.
drills.why: This exercise connects a deliberate opening with movement through it. Check the final shape before committing.
drills.reflect: Did the opening match your plan and leave enough room for the movement?

edit_guide.note: Crosshair on the ring in the centre tile, then edit. The window is the centre tile only.

drills.name: Window edit and peek
drills.tip: Edit the window, peek out on your right-hand side, and shoot the dummy behind the wall.
drills.why: A window gives you a sightline while the rest of the wall still covers you. The point of the edit is the shot you take through it, so the drill ends on a hit.
drills.reflect: Did you aim at the dummy before the window opened, or after?

drills.name: Arch edit
drills.tip: Create the intended arch opening, confirm it, and move through without a corrective edit.
drills.why: This exercise links a wider opening with controlled movement. Inspect the final shape rather than rushing the selection.
drills.reflect: Did the finished opening match the route you intended to take?

edit_guide.note: Start in the top-left tile and drag right between the two red lines, release in the top-right tile.

drills.name: Half-wall edit and jump shot
drills.tip: Take the top half off, jump, and shoot the dummy standing behind the wall.
drills.why: A half wall keeps your legs covered and opens a line above it. A jump shot lifts you into that line for a moment, which is when the shot has to land.
drills.reflect: Did you shoot at the top of your jump or on the way down?

edit_guide.note: Crosshair on the ring in the centre tile before you press edit; no travel needed.

drills.name: Edit + reset
drills.tip: For this exercise, make the opening and reset it after the peek while returning to cover.
drills.why: Resetting practises closing the sightline you opened. In a fight, also check whether moving would be safer.
drills.reflect: Were you behind cover while the wall was returning to its closed shape?

drills.name: Claim the wall
drills.tip: Check that you control the intended wall before relying on its edit, then recover cover.
drills.why: This exercise links piece control with a planned opening. Owning a wall does not remove the need to track the opponent.
drills.reflect: Did you confirm control and the threat position before opening the wall?

edit_guide.note: Rest the crosshair on the ring in the right-middle tile before editing; peek from the side, not the middle.

drills.name: Edit, peek, reset
drills.tip: Peek from a side tile, not the obvious middle. Fire once at the dummy, reset, and never repeat the same timing.
drills.why: Starting near the target reduces correction during exposure. Repeat the setup to learn it, then vary timing and angle as the threat changes.
drills.reflect: How far did you move your crosshair after exposing yourself, and did you recover cover?

drills.name: Gun swap, shoot
drills.tip: Select the intended gun with your normal controls, settle the crosshair on the target, then fire.
drills.why: This exercise links a deliberate item swap with a controlled shot. The input sequence depends on your layout.
drills.reflect: Was the intended gun ready before you committed to the shot?

drills.name: Pickaxe and gun
drills.tip: Select the intended tool for each target and avoid unnecessary item changes between actions.
drills.why: Practising the transition between breaking and shooting reduces corrections while keeping attention on the target.
drills.reflect: Which transition needed an extra correction or pulled your crosshair away?

drills.name: Build, swap, shoot
drills.tip: After placing the wall, select the intended gun, aim at the target, and fire from useful cover.
drills.why: This exercise connects a build with a shot. Check both the selected item and your exposure during the transition.
drills.reflect: Was the gun ready and the crosshair on target before you exposed yourself?

practice_court.build_instruction: Copy the ghost pieces. Check each intended cell and orientation, then compare your placements with the guide.
practice_court.rebox_instruction: Choose a threat direction. Cover it as you move into the next cell, then check the sides and your escape route.
practice_court.peek_instruction: Start behind cover with your crosshair at target height. Open a right-hand angle, shoot, then return to cover.
practice_court.free_instruction: Choose one skill and repeat the setup. Inspect placement and exposure, then increase speed when the result is reliable.

adaptive_edit.title: EDIT ROUTES
adaptive_edit.reference: Aim guide only - not selected edit tiles
adaptive_edit.trace: Trace the numbered tiles; confirm, then reset.
adaptive_edit.reselect: Look off the wall briefly to choose another route.
